test_assurance_observations.title: Existing mount can satisfy the rejected-release-hash fallback assertion
test_assurance_observations.finding: About.test.tsx first renders an App without a usable entry script and waits for the unavailable-hash message. The same test then renders a second App with a rejecting fetch and checks only that a global screen.findAllByText query returns more than zero unavailable-hash messages. renderApp and renderWith do not unmount the earlier root; cleanup is registered only after each test. The first, already-confirmed message can therefore satisfy the second assertion even if the rejecting-fetch instance remains loading or fails to render the intended fallback.
test_assurance_observations.impact: This particular assertion does not independently establish the rejected entry-script-fetch fallback. It does not establish an application defect, a runtime test failure, or a repository-wide absence of release-hash coverage.
test_assurance_observations.remediation: Unmount the first App before the rejecting-fetch case, split the cases, or retain the second RenderResult and scope the awaited fallback assertion with within(second.container). Also observe the rejecting fetch call so that the intended path is exercised.

review_summary: ContextHelp tests assert keyboard focus, Escape, hover/tap dismissal ordering, safe text rendering, independent descriptions, and field-associated help while disabled. ErrorBoundary tests assert fixed redacted copy, route reset ownership, Back recovery and reload callback.

Payment request/proof and printable-bill tests assert URI families, invalid-request refusal, testnet caution, proof disclaimers and explicit reveal, oversized QR fallback, passphrase/bearer distinctions, fixed-token versus seller-stated fiat display, and print lifecycle. Source-string print CSS assertions do not establish real print layout.

QR tests assert secret reveal scope binds to kind, text and multipart bytes; changed secret payloads hide immediately, equivalent arrays and label changes do not extend the deadline, page visibility hides secrets, and large dialogs retain warnings and focus behavior. Dynamic reduced motion stops auto-advance and requires a fresh opt-in. Locale changes preserve QR bytes and selected part.

Internationalization tests assert inert interpolation and rich-text values, prototype-named tag handling, message syntax/plurals/round-tripping, complete security-key classification, English fallback for draft or unknown security messages, registry-owned review authority, and no catalog metadata or pseudo-locale bypass. The message variant only spells the bidi character as a Unicode escape; the security-key variant adds explicit privacy/clipboard classifications.

Language/context/storage tests assert persistence, browser-default reset, blocked-storage messaging, catalog-load fallback, language and direction updates, pseudo-locale filtering, and locale fallback chains. About tests assert absent/invalid/rejected manifest disablement and error-detail redaction; Disclosure tests assert same-chain replacement and service changes hide old manifests and suppress late results.

Assigned historical Settings tests assert explicit endpoint persistence choices, session-only consent surviving failed form validation, settings exchange review/confirmation and invalidation, scan privacy bounds, network-policy acknowledgement, own-node refusal before adapter creation, failed-save preservation and cross-tab conflict handling. This assigned Settings blob is a historical variant, not a claim that it equals current main or candidate.

No new production vulnerability or behavior defect was established. One bounded informational test-assurance observation is separate from the unchanged seven canonical production findings. Preserve BROWSER-01 existing Pay route regression correction.
